consumption_highway_wh_per_km.notes: Test: 70 mph (113 km/h) steady, upper 50s to mid-60s F (about 15-18 C), dry, wheel size not stated, battery-side (car display, not confirmed) | 2023 Mach-E Premium AWD extended range (91 kWh usable; same generation and pack as our 2026 AWD ER). Article reports 3.1 mi/kWh over 285 mi: 1000 / (3.1 x 1.609344) = 200 Wh/km. Other tests seen: 2021 First Edition AWD ER 285 mi; 2021 RWD Route 1 18-inch 287.4 mi (no energy figure). | Main session: 3.1 mi/kWh is a rounded figure (197-204 Wh/km); the page states no kWh total. Our data lists 91 kWh usable.

supercharger_access.notes: Ford: adapter gives Tesla Supercharger access in the U.S. and Canada (programme from 29 Feb 2024; the cited Ford page names no model years, so eligibility of this model year is not shown by it; 2025 has the feature from the factory). Recorded: via adapter today.

charge_port.notes: Estimated: the 2026 Mach-E has a CCS1 port (InsideEVs) and Ford sells a NACS adapter (2025 spec sheet); the Supercharger adapter programme for 2024-2026 owners implies the same CCS1 port. No port change found across 2021-2026.
